subject.title: Remote gateway node pairing broken — node token scopes empty, approval flow incomplete

question: Should node-role token scopes and node-role rotation be owned exclusively by the upstream gateway while this repository limits its fix to precise diagnostics, recovery UX, and cross-repository end-to-end proof?
rationale: The Windows client consumes gateway-issued authorization and must not self-grant scopes, but maintainers need to define the permanent gateway/client ownership boundary and coordinated acceptance test.

options.title: Gateway contract plus client UX
options.body: Fix token issuance and node-role rotation upstream, then add only state-specific recovery guidance and live cross-repository proof here.

options.title: Approved compatibility fallback
options.body: Add a narrowly scoped Windows compatibility path only if maintainers determine that supported older gateways cannot provide the required role-token behavior.

recommendation.title: Gateway contract plus client UX
recommendation.body: Fix token issuance and node-role rotation upstream, then add only state-specific recovery guidance and live cross-repository proof here.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history most directly covers the node/device approval distinction and Windows-client pairing hardening that defines this boundary.
